# Fixtures

Golden captures of what the current scripts observably do, produced by
`tests/harness/` and asserted against by `tests/equivalence.rs`.

Fixtures are data, never test files (R29). One integration test file drives a
table of named cases; everything a case needs to be reproduced lives here.

## Layout

```
tests/fixtures/<component>/<case>/
    case.json              metadata and the full input manifest
    expected/<platform>.txt the observable, one file per platform
```

Per-platform expected files are deliberate. The scripts disagree across
platforms today — unborn HEAD renders differently on Windows than under bash —
and R20 resolves each divergence to one recorded behavior at U13. Until then the
fixture records what each platform actually does, rather than pretending they
already agree.

## `case.json`

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema` | format version of this file |
| `case`, `component` | the case's identity |
| `observable` | which of R31's four observables this fixture holds |
| `source_commit` | the commit whose scripts produced it (R33) |
| `clock` | pinned reference epoch; every `mtime_offset` is relative to it (R30) |
| `git_state` | the `states.json` state the repo was built into, or `null` |
| `payload` | the stdin payload, relative to `tests/harness/` |
| `args` | argv passed after the subcommand |
| `notify_config` | the config input, relative to `tests/harness/` (R30, R44) |
| `session_id` | the session id after the scripts' own sanitization |
| `inputs` | every state file supplied, with its intended modification time |
| `captured` | one row per platform that has been captured |

`source_commit`, `clock`, and `notify_config` are required on every fixture and
asserted by `tests/equivalence.rs`. Without all three a fixture cannot be
regenerated, which makes it an unfalsifiable claim rather than a golden file.

## Regenerating

```bash
tests/harness/capture.sh --component git-refresh
tests/harness/capture.sh --at <commit>     # regenerate a historical commit's fixtures
```

A fix that lands on `master` for an already-ported component is re-applied in
Rust and its fixtures regenerated by re-running the harness against the fixed
`master` commit, in the same commit that resolves the sync (R39).

Paths inside a fixture are placeholders — `{HOME}`, `{TMP}`, `{REPO}`,
`{ROOT}`, `{SCRIPTS}`. The harness refuses to write a capture that still
contains a real home path.
